To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the selection of decision strategies is an important determinant of the observed choices of consumers in SP experiments; (2) task complexity is an important determinant, but not the only one, of the decision strategies used by respondents; (3) the cognitive burden created by a sequence of choice scenarios is also important; (4) decision strategies are not independent from each other, but rather are correlated; (5) the decision strategies are not necessarily stable over time.
